note.text:
Most AI governance dashboards are built to answer one question: what already went wrong.

That's the wrong question. By the time a bias incident or breach shows up in the numbers, the underlying model has usually been drifting for weeks.

Error rates creep up. Complaints trickle in. Data distributions shift quietly in the background. None of that trips a lagging metric, because lagging metrics only fire once harm is confirmed.

The real governance work happens in the gap between those two lines — the stretch where a model is clearly degrading but hasn't yet caused a reportable event.

Committees that wait for the lagging spike are managing damage. Committees that act on the leading curve are managing risk. Build the dashboard, set the thresholds, and give someone the authority to pull the plug early.

The incident lands at week 8 — the warning started at week 1.
